title: Freeze CCP2 receiver-resource eligibility traces
description:
Scope: one receiver/resource event-trace family and its schema/manifest entries in /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/test/vectors/. Specify expected actions for common control windows, explicit data opportunities, owned grants, receiver commitments, half-duplex exclusions, priority arrivals during RX, anonymous assignments, collision repair, passband placement, finite demodulators and overlapping roots. Derive outcomes from explicit interval/resource tables rather than a copy of a production scheduler. No radio model, allocation algorithm or mandatory hopping feature is implemented here.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Prefer hand-specified finite traces over a general event-model framework. The same language-neutral traces will later be driven through production APIs and native integration paths.
acceptance_criteria: Each trace has bounded initial state, ordered external events, expected eligible/denied actions and resulting observable state. Independent event tables reject grant-without-RX, overlapping RX/TX, preempted commitments and impossible simultaneous one-radio channels. Assignment repair, not common hash rotation, explains resolved collisions; fallback remains contended. Channel-list length never establishes receiver or TX concurrency. Schema checks reject incomplete or unknown traces.
